about: Twenty photographs taken round the Canada Water dock (Canada Water lake), SE16, on the morning of 7 October 2026 and given to the project under CC0 by the owner. This file holds the hand-made part: what each photo shows, how each building was identified, the camera position evidence, the white calibration and the facade regions to rectify. The measurements are made by the logged operation rectify-facade-patches and the graph by lift-contrib-photos (magpie/cwplans/tools/contrib-photos.mjs). Skills: docklands-data-curation ('Contributed photos'), photo-view-reconstruction.
creator: danbri (project owner)
time: about 09:00 BST (08:00 UTC) on 7 October 2026 (owner: 'taken NOW'); the owner's phone map screenshot of the walk is timed 09:08:43 BST. The JPEG files carry no EXIF time, GPS or camera model
owner_words: i will supply more photos of canada water taken NOW near the Dock by the Library. I include one of some stickers on the library door for white calibration. Weather at 9am is overcast, light drizzle. Save these in usual place as my cc0 contribs.
files_as_delivered: JPEG originals, unchanged bytes (renamed only). Each has EXIF orientation, resolution, ExifVersion 0221, ColorSpace sRGB and SceneCaptureType only, and an embedded ICC profile 'Display P3' (Apple, 2022): the pixel values are Display P3, although the EXIF ColorSpace tag says sRGB. No date, time, GPS, make, model, lens or exposure tags.

weather.cache: Open-Meteo in the londat cache (cwplans/cache/runs/2026-10-07/live-2026-10-07T0843Z.json.gz, weather row for 08:30 UTC): 14.9 C, humidity 89 %, wind 14.4 km/h from 354 deg, gusts 29.5 km/h, cloud 100 %, precipitation 0.1 mm, WMO code 51 (light drizzle)
weather.light: diffuse: no shadows, no sunlit faces; the sun (behind cloud) was at azimuth 122 deg true, altitude 16 deg at 08:09 UTC (astronomy-engine, tools/view-mcp sunAt). Good light for facade colours: every face has about the same light, unlike the evening set cwlibrary

position_evidence.source: a screenshot of the owner's phone map app, EXIF time 2026-10-07 09:08:43 (BST). NOT STORED in either repository: it shows the map provider's imagery and map data, which are not the owner's to license, and the owner's profile picture. Only the position below, derived by us, is recorded
position_evidence.how: The blue position dot was located by laying the OSM outlines of the Canada Water lake (relation 18015947), the library, Dock X and Decathlon over the screenshot at the screenshot's own scale bar (50 m = 216 px, 4.33 px per metre, north up). The outlines fit the imagery to about 2 to 3 m. The app showed no accuracy circle larger than the dot (about 4 m radius); urban phone fixes are often 5 to 15 m off, so 10 m is our judged one-sigma.
position_evidence.where: on the plaza at the south corner of Decathlon (9 Maritime Street), about 2 m from its south-south-east face, 22 m east of the north-east corner of the dock
position_evidence.heading: the app's view cone pointed about west (280 deg, cone about 45 deg wide): this is the phone compass while the screenshot was taken, not the direction of a photo
position_evidence.per_photo: Each photo's camera note below is judged from its content (the faces seen, the bearings between identified buildings); only photo 01 has a solved camera. Several photos (03, 04, 07, 08, 09, 10, 11) were taken within about 60 m of the fix.

osm_extract: openstreetmap.fr greater_london-latest.osm.pbf (data as of 2026-10-01, fetched 2026-10-02; data-register osm_extracts osmfr-greater-london; magpie/cwplans/data/raw/docklands/), cut with osmium to -0.060,51.493,-0.038,51.503 and, for the photo 01 skyline, -0.032,51.495,-0.005,51.510. Face lengths and outward normals are from the OSM outlines.
model: magpie/cwplans/docklands/data/area.js built 2026-10-03 (sha256 29a3eb87...), keyed by docklands/data/building-keys.json: model index, height above the ground (height_m), ground (base_m_od), roof (top_m_od = base_m_od + height_m) and height source at that build.

calibration.what: Safety stickers on the glass entrance door of Canada Water Library (north face): 'CCTV in operation' (yellow on white), 'Automatic door' (black on white) and 'Keep clear' (blue on white). The white sign backgrounds are the white reference. The printed safety yellow and blue are secondary references only: their print colour is not known.

white.where: clean white areas of the 'Automatic door' sign, above the word Automatic and below the word door (pixel boxes x0 y0 x1 y1 in the stored photo)
white.cast: slightly yellow-green: b* +2.5 (blue 5 % low against green in linear light), a* -1.6; L* 86.6 (not clipped). As rendered, the white point is a little warmer and greener than D65 (x,y 0.3127, 0.3290); McCamy CCT of the rendered white about 6,330 K. This is the phone's processed result (auto white balance already applied), not a measurement of the daylight.

yellow_secondary.note: inside the CCTV triangle; out of the sRGB gamut (blue clips to 0)

calibration.sky_method: median of bright, low-chroma pixels (min channel > 150, max - min < 30) in the top 40 % of each photo; Display P3 values converted to CIELAB D65
how_to_use: Photo 19 itself: multiply linear-light R by 1.015 and B by 1.055 (decode the Display P3 values with the sRGB curve, scale, re-encode); the white sign then reads neutral.

The other photos: do not copy these gains blindly. The phone set white balance for each shot separately, so the cast differs from shot to shot. Balance each photo on a neutral in that photo (the overcast sky near the horizon, white paint such as Dock X's canopy columns, the white van in 03 and 04) and use photo 19 to check the method and the size of the error.

Size of the error: the overcast sky came out within 4 units of neutral in every photo (a* -3.8 to 0.0, b* -2.9 to +1.3) and the white sign at b* +2.5, so colours read from these photos are within about 3 to 5 CIELAB units of a balanced result. That is good enough for brick, render and metal tones.
Before any colour is measured, convert from Display P3 to sRGB with the embedded profile (fault F51): read as sRGB, red-brown brick is wrong by about 6 CIELAB units; the neutrals by less than 1.
The sticker is vinyl on the glass of the door, under the library's overhang; some warm interior light may pass through it. A white card held in open light would be a better reference next time.
